architecture_boundary: UnifiedDB is one canonical authority substrate with multiple typed subsystem writers.
PRAGMA main.data_version is database-wide for commits observed from another connection and therefore cannot itself identify mutation of WP206-owned state.
The persistent_agency_kernel contract explicitly separates UnifiedDB file identity from Agency checkpoint state identity.

Repository-hosted executable counterevidence invalidates only the proposed G6 hard-data_version acceptance semantics; it does not invalidate accepted G5/G4/G3 scopes and mints no target-runtime credit.

do_not: Do not retain data_version inequality as an unconditional hard failure in the shared UnifiedDB runtime.
Do not substitute the whole-file UnifiedDB fingerprint as the WP206 state witness because legitimate unrelated subsystem commits change the shared database.
Do not grant an implicit exclusive-writer epoch to WP206 without an explicit architecture contract and executable integration proof.
bounded_mechanism: Keep device/inode/path authority checks as hard file-identity fences.
Treat a changed connection-local data_version only as evidence that some other connection committed.
Recompute a deterministic witness over WP206-owned durable state/schema only, including f2_persistent_agency_checkpoints and the WP206 legacy-recovery authority surface when present.
If the WP206-owned witness is unchanged, accept the unrelated UnifiedDB commit, advance the local data_version observation baseline, and continue.
If the WP206-owned witness changed without the store's admitted same-connection mutation path, fail closed with a WP206-owned-state drift error.
After every admitted same-connection WP206 commit or migration/recovery commit, refresh the owned-state witness baseline explicitly.

Fence revalidation races: bind the witness to a stable observation window or re-read data_version after witness computation and retry/fail closed if another external commit occurred during revalidation.
